## Consumer need

A fresh ESM consumer using pnpm should have a documented route to install `microdelta@0.2.0` and use its current private-alpha durable workspace. The native SQLite dependency requires local build approval under pnpm; the repository's getting-started material does not explain this prerequisite.

This is an installation/documentation gap. Alpha remains project-private, and the package manager's build approval is working as designed. It is separate from #154's TypeScript declaration configuration.

## Minimal reproduction

On macOS arm64, Node 24.22.1, create a fresh directory with this `package.json`:

```json
{"name":"consumer","private":true,"type":"module","dependencies":{"microdelta":"0.2.0"}}
```

And `open.mjs`:

```js
import { openWorkspace } from 'microdelta';
const workspace = openWorkspace({ location: './history.sqlite', logicalStore: 'consumer' });
workspace.close();
```

Run `pnpm install`, then `node open.mjs`.

Observed:

- **pnpm 10.34.7:** install exits 0 with `Ignored build scripts: better-sqlite3@12.9.0`; durable open fails with `Could not locate the bindings file`.
- **pnpm 12.10.1:** install exits 1 with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` naming `better-sqlite3`.
- Importing the ESM package and using the public memory store works; this is not an ESM resolution failure.

Expected: documentation names the native prerequisite and gives a targeted, tested approval/rebuild recipe so users do not discover it only at durable open or assume their TypeScript/ESM setup is broken.

## Positive control and evidence

For these tested pnpm versions, a local `pnpm-workspace.yaml` containing:

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  better-sqlite3: true
```

followed by `pnpm rebuild better-sqlite3` makes both isolated consumers work. A durable cold run executes once and publishes; a second independent process executes zero bodies and reuses the same exact reference. pnpm also offers its interactive `pnpm approve-builds` command. No global relaxation is needed.

Reproduction branch `gap-hunt-durability`, commit [`447d798c7bd65b1d09e597dbdec1eb5f6944bb06`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/447d798c7bd65b1d09e597dbdec1eb5f6944bb06): [fixtures, replay instructions and captured install/cold/restart logs](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/tree/447d798c7bd65b1d09e597dbdec1eb5f6944bb06/scratch/gap-hunt/portability).

## Severity and suggested direction

Medium DX. Add native-dependency and supported-package-manager setup guidance, linked from the facade/example entry points, with a fresh external ESM smoke test. Keep Node-version compatibility separate: these controls are Node 24 evidence and establish no Node 26 or Linux support.

## Implementation contract and queue handoff

Pickup-ready for documentation and bounded verification only. Fixed portable reproduction branch `gap-hunt-durability@0683c2ed73934d10f9b5a1ad9e0dd9e3d1a88d4f`. No runtime support policy, driver or engine-range change is included.

Consumer need: a fresh external ESM consumer must discover the local native-build prerequisite before durable open, with a targeted recipe reachable from the root getting-started, facade README and contribution example. This is documentation and a bounded acceptance fixture, not a pnpm defect.

Numbered acceptance criteria:

1. Document better-sqlite3's native build prerequisite and tested pnpm10.34.7/12.10.1 differences. Distinguish public memory-store support from project-private alpha durable usage.
2. Give consumer-local `allowBuilds: {better-sqlite3: true}` YAML plus `pnpm rebuild better-sqlite3`, or an equivalently verified targeted approval workflow. Do not recommend global bypasses or approving unrelated dependencies.
3. Preserve negative controls: unapproved pnpm10 install warns then durable open fails for missing bindings; pnpm12 install rejects ignored builds. Public ESM memory smoke succeeds. Do not misdiagnose these as #154 TypeScript failures.
4. After local approval, cold durable work executes once/publishes; a separate Node process executes zero bodies/reuses the exact reference. Include the fixture and captured command results in implementation evidence.
5. Link native Node support guidance tracked in #158 without claiming untested Node26 or Linux runtime support.

Clean evidence-checkout Linux acceptance command (repository root):

```sh
bash scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/verify-157.sh
```

The portable runner is self-contained, accepts Node24.x (macOS controls were captured on24.22.1), pins pnpm versions and published microdelta0.2.0, creates/removes disposable external consumers/stores, and never edits global trust settings. Prerequisites: fresh Linux user/container without inherited pnpm approvals, Node24.x/npm, Bash, network/npm registry access, and Python3/make/g++ if native prebuild fallback is needed. The caller supplies Linux for Linux acceptance; the same runner can execute on macOS and does not create a container. Optional argument selects10.34.7 or12.10.1.

Verification boundary: Linux execution is still required. See verify-157.log for the fresh macOS runner result; do not infer Linux support from it. Underlying macOS install/approval/cold/restart evidence is in `scratch/gap-hunt/portability/REPORT.md` at447d798. Evidence scripts are on the worker branch and must be carried into a clean evidence checkout before invocation; they are not claimed to exist on main.

Blocking dependencies: none. Coordinate support wording with #158; #154 is independent. Out of scope: package publication, engine changes, driver changes, Node26 expansion, automatic build-trust relaxation and alpha promotion.

Fresh macOS manager download boundary: pnpm10 runner completed; a freshly installed pnpm12 executable was killed before package installation (137), so that run did not establish the expected approval rejection. Optional `PNPM12_BIN` selects an existing exact12.10.1 executable and the runner validates its version. This is an explicit environment prerequisite fallback, not a global trust change or an explanation of the kill. The default clean Linux invocation remains to be executed.

These checks diagnose the immutable published0.2.0 release. Any implementation documentation must state which published version it describes; no package mutation/publication is part of this pickup.

Fresh macOS fallback result: both manager versions passed unapproved negative controls, public memory smoke and approved cold1/published then independent restart0/reused exact reference. `verify-157.log` captures the result. This run used `PNPM12_BIN` pointing to the existing exact12.10.1 executable; it does not validate default fresh pnpm12 launch.

## Linux parity update (2026-10-23)

The owner-provided Linux aarch64 report states “Both main-branch full npm test runs passed” and “All 8 isolated installs and all 8 full builds passed.” Main `c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6` successfully installed native dependencies, built and ran full `npm test` on Node24.13.0 and Node26.12.1 with independently installed bindings.

Those runs used **npm**, not the pnpm10/12 approval scenarios in this issue. They establish working native installation/runtime on the tested Linux hosts and refute a blanket Node26 incompatibility claim; they do not resolve or contradict pnpm's targeted local build-approval prerequisite. The pnpm-specific Linux command remains unexecuted in the supplied matrix. #158 records the observed macOS SDK linker failure alongside Linux success. Its later macOS control also builds the locked driver successfully using a consistent command-local CLT compiler/linker/SDK and passes both Node24/26 shared-store sequences; this does not test pnpm approval. See the [toolchain evidence](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/6d3f3f3/scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/node26-clt/REPORT.md). Keep package-manager trust policy separate from native platform/toolchain failure.

## Attribution

Implementer: Codex worker (`gpt-6.1-sol`), operating for Mike North.
Agent assistance: The worker performed the isolated installs and positive controls; the supervising Codex agent reviewed the fixtures/logs and classification, checked existing issues, and filed this finding. No human implementation or review is claimed.

title: Document native SQLite build approval for pnpm 10/12 consumers
